messages:
audit-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GCS bucket 'redwood-logs-archive' has an IAM binding granting roles/storage.objectViewer to allUsers (detected). Public-access prevention not enforced.

sofia (sec-lead): acknowledged. tagging @jason @priya — please triage and contain. tagging @maria for legal awareness.

jason (infra): on it. removing public binding now. running quick commands:
```
gsutil iam ch -d allUsers:roles/storage.objectViewer gs://redwood-logs-archive
gcloud storage buckets update gs://redwood-logs-archive --public-access-prevention enforced
```

priya (sre): I'll pull access logs and check for object GETs from external IPs. running a narrow query on logging.

jason (infra): done — removal applied and public-access-prevention enabled. pushed a hotfix commit to infra repo: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/commit/3a7b9 (hotfix). :white_check_mark:

priya (sre): initial log search shows a handful of GETs from IPs not in our allowlist between 2026-05-02T21:00 and 2026-05-03T02:00 UTC. saving details to incident ticket.

priya (sre): command used:
```
gcloud logging read 'resource.type=\"gcs_bucket\" AND resource.labels.bucket_name=\"redwood-logs-archive\" AND protoPayload.methodName:(\"storage.objects.get\" OR \"storage.objects.getIamPolicy\")' --limit 200
```

maria (legal): thanks for the ping. please add a summary of potentially accessed object names and any PII findings to the ticket. we'll evaluate notification obligations.

jason (infra): looks like the public grant originated from a terraform apply in module tf-storage-lifecycle. suspect an empty var caused policy to default to allUsers. opening a rollback PR and a followup to fix the module. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/987 (rollback + guardrail).

sofia (sec-lead): action: rotate creds for backup SA and any service accounts that had access to that bucket. @jason assignable?

jason (infra): assigning to myself. rotating keys for backup-sa and redeploying. will also update the TF module to explicitly deny allUsers binding and add a pre-apply check.

priya (sre): scanned object list for sensitive markers; flagged 2 objects with hashed tokens (no clear PII) and one archived debug dump that may contain config snippets. marking for deeper review.

maria (legal): please redact full object contents in ticket; send sample to legal privately if anything suspicious.

sofia (sec-lead): containment checklist so far: removed IAM binding, enforced public access prevention, rotated SA keys (in progress), opened rollback PR, logging/forensics running, legal notified. Assign follow-ups and owners in the incident ticket. :clipboard:

jason (infra): SA keys rotated and backup service redeployed. Terraform guard added (deny-allusers) and CI policy added to infra pipeline to fail on allUsers bindings. PR merged.

priya (sre): forensic notes: downloaded object access count = 18 distinct objects, 3 external IPs. saving indicators to the ticket. starting an object integrity snapshot to object-storage-repro for deeper analysis.

sofia (sec-lead): comms: draft for customer-facing support and internal exec blurb prepared. awaiting final legal signoff. will not send external notice yet until we confirm sensitive data exposure.

maria (legal): reviewed draft; ok with internal exec note, hold customer notice pending deeper review.

sofia (sec-lead): next steps: 1) postmortem on Tue 2026-05-05 1400 UTC, 2) retro-fit TF guardrails across all storage modules, 3) add automated smoke test that verifies public-access-prevention for prod buckets, 4) include this scenario in oncall runbook. owners: jason/priya/legal.

deploy-bot: created channel #incident-1865001234 and Jira INC-186500 for tracking. invited participants.

jason (infra): quick note — found a secondary bucket in a staging project with a similar misconfig in an outdated module. patching that now.

sofia (sec-lead): good catch. add to incident scope. thanks everyone. reconvene after forensics update. :thumbsup:
